text:
Maya: Quick sync: onboarding model-rank-v3-quant-int8 as our expensive reranker in a two-stage pipeline (BM25 -> NN). Goal: keep p99 latency <= 120ms and avoid >0.01 drop in golden NDCG@10. Need an evaluation plan that ties quality to cost.
Ravi: Offline replay is the only safe first step. Replay 2 weeks of traffic, log which queries would escalate to NN under different cascade policies, and simulate measured per-request NN latency distribution.
Sofia: Add a calibration pass: quantization may change score magnitudes and ordering. Run full-precision vs int8 on a curated golden set (2k queries, diverse languages). Compute ndcg_full, ndcg_int8, and per-query rank-deltas.
Ken: For cascade policies: compare three axes -> topk (50,100,200), score-gap (0.05,0.1,0.2), and combined (topk + gap). We'll sweep grid and produce a pareto frontier of NDCG@10 vs p99 latency.
Maya: How do we estimate p99 from offline runs?
Ravi: Use measured NN latency histogram from canary infra (samples by qps and batch size). For each replayed NN call, sample latency from that histogram conditioned on batch size; compute end-to-end latency per query including BM25 time. Then compute p50/p95/p99.
Sofia: Stats needed: per-config NDCG@10, MRR, #NN_calls_per_1M, avg_tokens_in, estimated_gpu_token_cost, and golden_ndcg_delta. Also bootstrap CIs (1000 resamples).
Ken: Suggest a "costed-NDCG" metric: costed_ndcg = ndcg - lambda * (p99_ms / 1000). lambda tuned to $/sec unit so it reflects budget. We'll show multiple lambdas (low/medium/high).
Maya: Any guardrails for weird slices?
Sofia: Yes: surface top 500 queries by ndcg drop (fullNN - cascade). Flag slices where >5% of queries have drop>0.05. Also check long-doc (>1024 tokens) and low-click docs.
Ravi: Implementation snippet: 
```
# simulate cascade
for q in replay_queries:
  candidates = bm25(q, k=200)
  if cascade_policy(candidates):
    latency = sample_latency(batch_size_for_q)
    rerank_scores = reranker_int8.score(candidates)
  else:
    rerank_scores = shallow_score(candidates)
  compute_ndcg(q, rerank_scores)
```
Ken: Make sure the cascade decision is deterministic in the replay (use the same BM25 scoring seed) so comparisons are paired.
Maya: What sample sizes do we need for stable ndcg deltas?
Sofia: For small deltas (~0.005) you need ~20k queries. For larger effects ~5k can detect. We'll default to 20k unique queries per grid cell.
Ravi: Also: simulate traffic skew. Under peak qps batch sizes grow and latency distribution changes. Run two traffic profiles: median and peak.
Ken: Cost calc: tokens_in_per_call * per_token_gpu_cost + overhead_per_call. Translate to $/1M queries. We'll include Dedicated vs Hosted price knobs.
eval-bot: eval-run 448 queued: cascade-grid (topk:50-200, gap:0.05-0.2) using replay window 2026-02-01..2026-02-14. ETA ~3h.
Maya: Awesome. Ravi owns replay infra, Sofia owns golden set & CI tests, Ken owns costed-NDCG plots. Drop CSVs to /shared/benchmarks/rerank/onboard-1752469000 and ping.
Maya: small follow-up: include language tag in outputs so we can filter non-en and see if quant has asymmetric effects.
Sofia: noted. We'll also track tokenization mismatches (token counts) and a small sanity check: boolean flag if top-1 changed for golden queries.
Maya: thanks team :rocket:
